question: Can I edit GRBL settings from the app?

question: How do I read all my controller's current settings?

question: How do I restore my controller to factory GRBL defaults?

question: How do I load a G-code file?

question: What G-code file types are supported?

question: Is the Project tab where I load a new file?

question: Can I load a file from a saved library instead of my computer?

question: How do I keep a copy of my G-code file for later?

question: Why won't my G-code file load?
answer: Check the Console for the reason. The file must be .nc, .gcode, .txt, .ngc, .cnc or .tap, no larger than 50 MB, and contain G-code (empty or comment-only files are refused). You can't load, reload or clear a file while a carve is running or paused, so press Stop in the Carve control bar first. question: Does loading a file automatically show it in the 3D viewer?

question: Where does a newly loaded file show up afterward?

It's also added to the Project tab's list when you open that tab while the file is loaded, and the same file (same name and size) isn't added twice.

question: Can I watch a folder for new G-code files automatically?
answer: Yes. In Settings > Hardware > Watch folder, tick Enable folder watching, enter the Folder path and Extensions (comma separated), and click Save. Matching files are listed under "Files currently in folder" (click the refresh button to update the list). There's no Load button there, so you still load files through File Management or the Library.

question: How large a G-code file can I load?
answer: Up to 50 MB; larger files are refused with "File too large" in the Console. Very large files take longer to read. If a file has more than 100,000 toolpath segments, the Console shows "Segment cap hit" because some display data was thinned out for the 3D view; the file sent to the machine isn't changed.

question: How do I start my job?
answer: Load your file, open the Carve tab, and press the Start (play) button at the left end of the job control bar along the bottom of the 3D view; in the vertical touchscreen layout it's the Start key in the Job control card under the view. You can also press Space when the machine is idle and a file is loaded. If a stopped job left a saved resume line, the bar shows "continues from line N" and Start picks up from that line instead of the beginning.
aliases: how do I press go on my file

question: How do I pause a running job?
answer: Press the play button on the Carve tab's job control bar, which turns into Pause while the job runs, or press Space. The machine holds where it is; press the button (it shows Start again while paused) or Space to carry on.
aliases: hold the cut for a moment

question: How do I stop a job?
answer: Press the square Stop Job button on the Carve tab's job control bar, or press Esc. On RSP controllers the line it stopped at is saved, so Start can continue from there later. In an emergency use the red E-STOP button instead.

question: Is there a Start/Pause/Stop button panel?
answer: Yes. On the Carve tab a job control bar sits along the bottom of the 3D view (a Job control card under the view in the vertical layout) with Start/Pause, a Lines / Current / % progress readout, Run Outline, Start From Line, Stop Job and E-STOP. It appears once a file is loaded, and whenever a job is running or paused.

question: Why can't I find a Start button for my job?
answer: The Start button is only on the Carve tab and only appears after a G-code file is loaded; the Prepare tab has a Simulate button instead, which never moves the machine. If you can see the bar but Start is greyed out, the machine isn't connected, it's in alarm, or the loaded file was refused (hover over the button to see why).

question: Can I resume a job after pausing?
answer: Yes. Press the play button on the job control bar (it shows Start while paused) or press Space, and the job continues from where it held. If the job was stopped rather than paused, on RSP controllers Start continues from the saved line: the tool lifts, travels back and plunges before cutting.
aliases: carry on cutting after a hold

question: What happens if I press Escape during a job?
answer: Esc sends Stop, the same as the Stop Job button: the job ends and, on RSP controllers, the stop line is saved so Start can continue later. It works whenever the machine is connected and you aren't typing in a text box.

The Space shortcut, however, starts a loaded file from any tab when the machine is idle, so avoid pressing it by accident. Once a job is running or paused, every header tab except Carve is locked.

question: How do I control coolant during a job?

question: How do I control the spindle or laser during a job?
answer: Use the Sidebar's Controls sub-tab, which stays open during a carve: the Spindle / Laser section has Spindle mode (Speed (RPM), CW, CCW, Stop) and Laser mode (Power, ON, OFF, Test Fire). On RSP controllers spindle and laser control isn't supported, so start and stop your router yourself.

question: How do I override my feed rate while running?

question: How do I home my machine?
answer: On Prepare or Carve, open the Sidebar's Position tab and click HOME ALL, or press the Home key on your keyboard while connected. The house icon next to the logo in the header only opens the Home menu; it doesn't home the machine. Homing is refused while a job is running or paused, so stop the job first.

question: Can I home just one axis?

question: What's the keyboard shortcut to home the machine?

question: What order do the axes home in?

question: How do I cancel homing mid-way?

question: Does the homing overlay close automatically?

question: Is there a home option in the Home menu dropdown besides Home All?

question: What's the difference between Work Position and Machine Position?

question: What do I do if my machine shows an alarm?

question: How do I clear a limit switch trip?
answer: In the alarm popup, click Clear Limit. On RTS controllers it stops motion, resets all four motors and unlocks; on RSP controllers it sends the same unlock as Clear Alarm. Once the popup closes, jog the axis away from the switch.

question: What does Reset Motors do?
answer: Reset Motors appears in the popup only for a MOTOR ERROR ('Closed-loop position error detected. Check motor wiring.'). It resets all four motors (X, Y1, Y2, Z); click Details to reset just one. On RSP controllers it sends the same unlock as Clear Alarm.

question: Where else can I clear an alarm besides the popup?

The Sidebar's Position tab shows an alarm banner with Reset X, Reset Y1, Reset Y2, Reset Z and Reset All, and the Jog tab shows Reset X, Reset Y, Reset Z and Reset All. question: What does the ALARM badge in the status bar do?

question: How do I see which specific axis or motor caused the alarm?

question: My machine won't move and there's no visible error -- what should I check?

question: What is the Z runaway abort warning?

It shows the drop, time, threshold and current machine Z, and tells you to power-cycle and re-home before resuming. It closes after 60 seconds or with its × button.

question: What does 'WCS health check failed' mean?
answer: It's a yellow banner shown on RTS controllers when the active G54 offset on any axis is beyond ±50 mm, which usually means the stored offset got corrupted. Home, click Zero All at the homed position, and power-cycle before running any G-code. The × closes the banner.

question: What is a 'Pre-flight BLOCKED' message?
answer: It's a banner meant to block Start when a toolpath goes outside the machine's travel, but the app doesn't run that check in this build, so you normally won't see it. Before running, check the file card on the Prepare tab's 3D view, which shows 'In Range' or 'Exceeds Travel Limit' for the selected machine size.

question: Can I override a Pre-flight BLOCKED warning?
answer: The banner has an '⚠️ Arm one-shot override' button that lets only the next Start skip the check. Since the pre-flight check isn't active in this build, there's normally nothing to override; use the Prepare tab's In Range / Exceeds Travel Limit badge to check fit instead.

question: Why does my alarm keep coming back after I clear it?
answer: The cause is still active: an E-stop button still pressed (RSP controllers won't leave E-stop until it's released), a limit switch still held, something binding, or a motor driver fault. Fix it, then click Clear Alarm. If a driver alarm won't clear, power-cycle the machine, then home or re-zero, because a restart loses position.

question: What's the difference between an alarm and a motor error?
answer: An ALARM (orange popup) means the controller locked itself, for example from an E-stop, limit or fault; clear it with Clear Alarm. A MOTOR ERROR (red popup) means a closed-loop motor lost its position; clear it with Reset Motors, or open Details to reset one motor (X, Y1, Y2 or Z). On RSP controllers every one of these buttons sends the same unlock.

question: Does the app warn me before letting me run a job with a bad origin?

On RTS controllers a 'WCS health check failed.' banner warns about offsets beyond ±50 mm. After a controller restart the app does block Start until you re-zero X, Y and Z or home.

question: How do I turn on coolant?

question: How do I turn off coolant?
answer: Press the lit Mist or Flood button again, or press Stop (M9) in the Coolant section of the Controls sub-tab. Stop is greyed out when the app thinks coolant is already off. On RSP controllers coolant commands aren't sent at all, so switch coolant off at the machine.

question: What's the difference between Mist and Flood coolant?
answer: Mist sends M7 and Flood sends M8, which drive separate coolant outputs on the controller. Use whichever one your coolant system is wired to.

question: Where is the coolant control?

question: Can I run mist and flood coolant at the same time?
answer: The Coolant panel only tracks one mode at a time: pressing Flood while Mist is on sends M8 and switches the badge to FLOOD, but it doesn't send an off command for mist. On controllers that support both outputs both may therefore be running, so press Stop (M9) to turn all coolant off.

question: Does stopping a job also stop coolant?
answer: The app doesn't send a coolant-off command when you stop a job, and the Coolant panel doesn't change by itself. Whether coolant shuts off depends on the controller, so check after stopping and press Stop (M9) if it's still running.

question: Is there a coolant status indicator?

question: How do I turn on my spindle?

question: How do I stop the spindle?
answer: Press Stop (M5) in the Spindle / Laser section of the Controls sub-tab; it's only enabled while the app shows the spindle as running. On RSP controllers the stop command isn't sent to the board, so switch the spindle or router off physically.

question: How do I set spindle RPM?
answer: Type a value in Speed (RPM) or drag the slider below it (0 to 24,000 in steps of 100) in the Spindle / Laser section of the Controls sub-tab. The new speed is only sent when you press CW or CCW, so press it again if the spindle is already running.

question: How do I switch to laser mode?

question: What does test-fire do in laser mode?

question: Can I run the spindle in reverse?

question: Where do I set max spindle RPM for my machine?

question: Is spindle RPM control available during a running job?

question: Is feed override available before I start a job, or only during?

question: What's a safe way to slow down mid-cut if something looks wrong?

question: Where do I see the 3D toolpath of my G-code?

question: How do I open the 3D viewer?

question: Can I rotate/pan/zoom the 3D view?

question: Why don't I see my toolpath in the 3D view?

question: Is there a 2D toolpath preview as an alternative to the 3D view?

question: Can I measure distances in the 3D viewer?

question: How do I edit a macro?

question: How do I delete a macro?

question: Are there built-in preset macros?

question: Will my macros still be there if I reload the page?

question: Can a macro run while the machine is disconnected?

question: Can I give a macro an icon or category?

question: What kind of commands can I put in a macro?
answer: Any G-code or M-code lines your controller accepts, one per line, such as a park move or a move to your tool-change position. The lines are sent as typed commands, so on controllers that don't accept typed G-code (such as RSP firmware) macro lines have no effect.

question: Is there a limit to how many macros I can create?

question: Can macros take parameters or variables?

question: How fast does a macro run through its commands?

question: Where would I put a 'go to tool-change position' macro?

question: Can I reorder my macros?

question: Do macros show up in the console log when run?

question: How do I send a raw G-code command manually?

question: Where is the console?

question: Does the console have command history I can scroll through with arrow keys?

question: What do the different colors and icons in the console log mean?

question: Does the console only show commands I type, or everything?

question: Can I collapse the console log?

question: Does the console auto-scroll?

question: Can I clear the console log?

question: What's the console useful for that the rest of the UI doesn't cover?

question: How do I switch my active WCS from the DRO?
answer: Device tab > Position (DRO) has a G54-G59 dropdown, enabled when connected. It changes the WCS the app shows as active, including in the status bar, but doesn't send a coordinate-system change to the controller.

question: Does the DRO show connection status?
answer: Yes. Device tab > Position (DRO) has a status badge at the bottom showing the machine state (for example IDLE, RUNNING or ALARM) when connected, or DISCONNECTED when not. A ● dot on the Position (DRO) section button also appears while connected.

question: Why do my typed DRO values not seem to move my zero point?
answer: You can't type values into the DRO in this build. To set your origin, jog to the spot and use ZERO ALL or the per-axis zero icons in the Sidebar's Position tab, or press Ctrl+Z.

question: What's in the Home menu dropdown at the top of the app?
answer: Click the house icon next to the Onefinity logo. It has three sections: Machine Information (Machine profile dropdown with Voltage and Work area), Device Info (Port, Manufacturer, Vendor ID and Baud Rate when connected, otherwise 'Not connected') and Ethernet (a 'Connect to IP' address). Click anywhere outside the panel to close it.
aliases: the menu next to the logo

question: Can I switch machine profiles from the Home menu?
answer: Yes. Home menu > Machine Information has a Machine profile dropdown; choosing one sets the active machine profile right away. It's the same setting as the dropdown in Device tab > CNC Controller > Machine Information.

question: How do I connect to my controller over Ethernet?
answer: This build has no button to connect over Ethernet. Home menu > Ethernet only stores a 'Connect to IP' address (default 192.168.5.1). Connect by USB in Device tab > CNC Controller instead.

question: Where do I see my connected port's vendor ID?
answer: Home menu > Device Info shows the connected Port, Manufacturer and Vendor ID, or 'Not connected'. The Baud Rate shown there is always 115200; if you connected manually, the Device Information card in Device tab > CNC Controller shows the rate actually used. The Device tab's port dropdown also lists VID and PID under each port.
aliases: which com port am I on

question: Is there a keyboard for typing the Ethernet IP on a touchscreen?
answer: Yes. Click the small keyboard icon ('Open on-screen keyboard') next to the 'Connect to IP' field in Home menu > Ethernet.

question: Does the Home menu let me home individual axes?
answer: No. The Home menu only has Machine Information, Device Info and Ethernet. Home axes from the Sidebar's Position tab (HOME ALL, or the house icon on each axis row) or press the Home key.
aliases: home x from the home menu
does the house menu home axes

question: Why were Probe settings removed from the Home menu?
answer: Probe settings aren't in the Home menu. Click the Probe button in the Sidebar tab bar (between Jog and Controls) to run the probing wizard, and see Settings > CNC > Probing for probe strategies.
aliases: probe options missing from home menu

question: What voltage/work-area info shows in Machine Information?
answer: Home menu > Machine Information shows Voltage and Work area for the selected machine profile when that profile has them. The Machine Information card in Device tab > CNC Controller also shows Max feed rate, Spindle, Controller and Notes. Fields left blank in a profile are hidden.

question: When does the on-screen keyboard appear?
answer: Only when you tap the keyboard icon next to the Connect to IP field. Open the Home menu (the house icon in the header), choose Ethernet, then tap the keyboard icon.
aliases: how to open on screen keys

question: Is the on-screen keyboard available on every text field?
answer: No. It's only available for the Connect to IP field in Home menu > Ethernet. Other fields, such as the Console and Macros, need a physical keyboard or your device's own touch keyboard.
aliases: on screen keyboard missing on other inputs
why no keyboard popup when I tap a field

question: How do I close the on-screen keyboard?
answer: Tap Close on its bottom row, or tap anywhere outside the keyboard and the IP field. It also closes when the Home menu closes.

question: What layout does the on-screen keyboard use?
answer: A number row (1 to 0, a dot and a backspace key), three rows of lowercase letters in QWERTY order, and a Close key. There's no space bar, Shift, Enter or other symbols.
aliases: what keys are on the touch keyboard

question: What keyboard shortcuts are available?
answer: Arrow keys jog X and Y, Page Up/Page Down jog Z, and 1 to 4 set the step to 0.1, 1, 10 or 100 mm. Space starts, pauses or resumes a job, Escape stops the job, the Home key homes all axes, Ctrl+O opens a file and Ctrl+Z zeros all axes. Shortcuts are ignored while you're typing in a field.

question: Where can I see the full list of shortcuts in the app?
answer: The app has no shortcuts help panel or button. The full list is: arrow keys and Page Up/Page Down to jog, 1 to 4 for step size, Space to start, pause or resume, Escape to stop, Home to home all axes, Ctrl+O to open a file and Ctrl+Z to zero all axes.

question: Do shortcuts work if I'm typing into a field?
answer: No. Shortcuts are ignored while a text box, text area or dropdown has focus, so typing in the Console or a macro can't move the machine. Click outside the field to use them again.
aliases: do hotkeys fire in text boxes

question: What key opens a file?
answer: Ctrl+O. It opens the same file picker as Browse for G-Code File on the Prepare or Carve tab.

question: What key zeros all axes?
answer: Ctrl+Z. It zeros X, Y and Z immediately with no confirmation (it isn't undo), and only while the machine is connected.

question: What key pauses my job?
answer: Space. It pauses a running job, resumes a paused one, and starts the loaded file when the machine is connected and idle.

question: What key stops my job?
answer: Escape. It sends a job Stop whenever the machine is connected and you're not typing in a field.

question: How do I jog Z with the keyboard?
answer: Page Up moves Z+ and Page Down moves Z- by the current step size. Hold the key to keep moving.

question: How do I change jog step size with the keyboard?
answer: Press 1 for 0.1 mm, 2 for 1 mm, 3 for 10 mm or 4 for 100 mm, and the matching button lights up in the Step (mm) row. There's no key for 50 mm.

question: Is there a shortcut to open the keyboard shortcuts help?
answer: No. The app has no shortcuts help panel, so no key opens one, and the ? key does nothing. Ask me "what keyboard shortcuts are available" to get the list.

question: Does holding an arrow key move continuously or just one step?
answer: A quick tap moves one step. Holding the key for more than about 350 ms starts continuous jogging, repeating about every 120 ms (one step each time) until you release it.

question: What is the safety warning banner at the top of the screen?
answer: It's a stack of warning cards at the very top of the app, above the header tabs, and it shows nothing while everything is healthy. It can show Controller restarted (RSP controllers), Z RUNAWAY ABORT and WCS health check failed (RTS controllers), and Pre-flight BLOCKED, which this version never triggers.

question: What types of safety warnings can the banner show?
answer: Controller restarted — position lost (Start blocked until you re-zero or home), Z RUNAWAY ABORT (the job was stopped because Z dropped too fast), WCS health check failed (a work offset beyond ±50 mm), and Pre-flight BLOCKED (an out-of-bounds check that isn't active in this version).

question: How do I dismiss a safety banner warning?
answer: Z RUNAWAY ABORT has an × button and also clears itself after 60 seconds, and WCS health check failed has an × to hide it. Controller restarted can't be dismissed: it clears once X, Y and Z are zeroed again or the machine is homed.
aliases: get rid of the red banner

question: What should I do after a WCS health check warning?
answer: Follow the banner: Home, click Zero All on the homed position, then power-cycle the controller before running any G-code. The warning means a G54 offset is beyond ±50 mm, which usually points to an offset corrupted in a previous session (RTS controllers).

question: What triggers a Pre-flight BLOCKED warning?
answer: Nothing in this version: the out-of-bounds pre-flight block is switched off, so this banner doesn't appear. On RSP controllers, files the machine can't run are refused when they load instead (Start greys out, and its tooltip and the Console give the reasons), and the Prepare tab's In Range / Exceeds Travel Limit badge gives a visual size check.
aliases: why was start blocked by preflight

question: Is Arm override safe to use?
answer: The "Arm one-shot override" button only appears on a Pre-flight BLOCKED banner, which this version doesn't show. When it is shown, it skips the pre-flight check for the next Start only (the Z watchdog stays active), so use it only if you're sure the block is a false alarm.

question: How large does a WCS offset error need to be to trigger the corrupt-offset warning?
answer: The WCS health check (RTS controllers) flags any G54 axis offset larger than ±50 mm. The separate "looks corrupted" note on the Pre-flight banner isn't raised in this version.
aliases: how big an offset is suspicious

question: Why did my job abort itself mid-cut with no error from me?
answer: Check the banner at the top and the Console. On RTS controllers a Z RUNAWAY ABORT stops the job if Z drops more than 20 mm within 3 seconds. On RSP controllers the Console names the reason and the line, such as a motor driver alarm, lost contact with the machine for about 15 seconds, no movement for 60 seconds, or a line the machine refused, and Start continues from that line once it's fixed. A controller restart or the PC going to sleep can also end a job.
aliases: why did the cut end early

question: Nothing happens when I click Connect -- what should I check first?
answer: Connect stays greyed out until you pick a port in 'Select a device...' and the Device tab shows Backend Online. If it tries and fails, read the red message and open Troubleshooting Tips: make sure the controller is powered and plugged in, close other CNC programs (UGS, bCNC, Candle, RTS-X) that may be holding the port, and try unplugging and replugging the USB cable. Also check Baud Rate and Flow Control match your controller.

question: My machine is connected but won't jog or run -- what's blocking it?
answer: Check the header pill: ALARM or MOTORERROR must be cleared first, and INITIALIZING means firmware is still being detected. Look for a 'Controller restarted — position lost' banner, which blocks Start until you re-zero X, Y and Z or home. Also check the Console for '⛔ ... not available while a job is running': jog, home and zero are blocked until you stop the job.

question: I loaded a file but the 3D view is empty -- why?
answer: Check that the sidebar's File Management shows the file name, size and line count, and that the file is a supported type (.nc, .gcode, .txt, .ngc, .cnc or .tap). The 3D view is only on the Prepare and Carve tabs, and a file with no readable G-code lines isn't loaded (look for a warning in the Console sub-tab).

question: How do I report a bug or missing feature in the software?
answer: There is no bug-report form in the app. Write down what you did, copy any error lines from the sidebar's Console sub-tab, and send them to whoever supports your machine or software.
aliases: something is broken who do I tell

question: Are there features in the code that aren't actually usable yet?
answer: A few: 'Run Again' in the Project tab does nothing and its Status stays 'Pending', the Library's 'Documentation' card is 'Coming soon', macros are not kept after the page reloads, and the tool library is only a reference list that nothing else reads. The Carve tab's job bar (Start/Pause, Stop, E-STOP) does work, and Space and Escape also start/pause and stop a job.

question: Is there a way to run the app fully offline?
answer: Yes for machine control: the software runs entirely on your own computer at http://localhost:4000 and talks directly to the connected machine. Internet is only needed for extras such as FILEFINITY, WhatsApp and Telegram, worldwide remote access and online firmware checks.

question: What port does the backend run on by default?
answer: Port 4000, so the app is at http://localhost:4000 on the computer running it. To use another port, open Command Prompt in the app folder and run set PORT=5000 && runtime\node.exe backend\index.js, then open http://localhost:5000.

question: Does the app support touchscreens?
answer: Yes. There is a vertical touchscreen layout with larger buttons; it turns on automatically on portrait or narrow screens, or you can pick it with the layout button in the header (Auto → Horizontal → Vertical). Some fields, such as the Ethernet IP in the Home menu, also have an on-screen keyboard button.

question: Can multiple people control the machine from different browsers at once?
answer: Several browsers and devices can have the app open at once and all see live status, and each remote device needs the PIN. The app does not stop two people from sending conflicting commands, so let only one person operate the machine at a time.

question: Where should I look first if something in the UI seems broken or unresponsive?
answer: Check the sidebar's Console sub-tab for error lines, look for an alarm popup, a warning banner or the ALARM badge in the bottom status bar, and confirm the Device tab still shows the machine as connected. If the whole app stopped responding, make sure the black server window started by RUN.bat is still open.

question: What should a new user do their very first time using this software?
answer: Start the software, go to the Device tab and connect to your machine, then home it (Sidebar > Position > 'HOME ALL'). question: What's in the Sidebar on the Prepare and Carve tabs?
answer: File Management is at the top for loading files. Below it is a row of sub-tabs: Position, Jog, Probe (a button that opens the probing wizard), Controls, Macros and Console. A camera panel sits at the bottom of the Sidebar.

question: Why can't I see the Sidebar?
answer: The Sidebar only appears on the Prepare and Carve tabs. In the horizontal layout it's to the left of the 3D view; in the vertical touchscreen layout it fills the left column.
aliases: where did the jog panel go

question: Which Sidebar sub-tab opens first?
answer: Position. The Sidebar goes back to Position whenever it's opened again, for example after you visit another top tab or reload the page.
aliases: why does it always show position

question: Why did the Sidebar switch to Controls on its own?
answer: If you're on the Jog sub-tab when a carve starts, the Sidebar moves you to Controls. Jog is locked during the carve, and Controls has the feed override you may want to adjust.
aliases: why am I on controls tab

question: What does the 'Carve in progress — file and jog locked' message mean?
answer: It appears in the Sidebar while a job is running or paused. Loading, reloading and clearing files and jogging are blocked so the running program can't be changed, but the Controls sub-tab stays open so you can change the feed rate. Stop the job to unlock everything.
aliases: why is everything locked during a cut

question: What does the gear icon next to File Management do?
answer: Nothing at the moment; it has no function. It's hidden on the vertical touchscreen layout.

question: Can I use the Controls sub-tab during a carve?
answer: Yes. Unlike Jog and File Management, the Controls sub-tab stays open while a job is running or paused, so you can adjust the feed override mid-carve.

question: What does the Probe button in the Sidebar tab row do?
answer: Probe isn't a sub-tab. Clicking it (crosshair icon, between Jog and Controls) opens the probing wizard at its first step, where you choose the probe type.

question: What does the Sidebar remember after a reload?
answer: The jog Step (mm) and Speed, the last loaded file, and the Sidebar and G-code panel widths are remembered in this browser. Macros, the Console log, the selected sub-tab, the mm/in readout choice and the layout choice are not.

question: Why is Browse for G-Code File greyed out?
answer: File loading is locked while a job is running or paused, and the file card says "File upload locked during carve". Press the Stop button in the Carve tab's job control bar, then load the new file.

question: How do I clear or unload the current file?
answer: Click the X icon (Clear file) on the file card in Sidebar > File Management. The file and its 3D preview are removed and the card goes back to "No file loaded". It's disabled while a carve is running or paused.

question: Is my loaded file remembered after I refresh the page?
answer: Yes. The last loaded file is kept in this browser and restored after a reload, and the Console shows "Restored ... G-code lines from last session". If a file is too large for the browser to store, it won't come back and you'll need to load it again.
aliases: does the app remember my job

question: Does loading a file start the job?
answer: No. Loading only reads the file, draws the preview and sends the program to the machine. Nothing moves until you press Play (Start) on the Carve tab or press Space.

question: Is the file sent to the machine when I load it?
answer: Yes, once the machine is connected and ready. If you load a file before connecting, it's sent automatically after the connection comes up. The Console shows "File loaded: name (N lines)" when the machine has it.

question: What does 'Loaded & Ready' on the file card mean?
answer: It means the file was read and previewed on this screen. It doesn't guarantee the machine accepted it, so check the Console for "File loaded" or a "cannot run on this machine" message.
aliases: is my file ready to run

question: What does 'cannot run on this machine' mean after loading a file?
answer: The machine checked the file, found problems and won't run it. The Console lists up to five of the problems, with line numbers where available. Fix them in your CAM software and load the file again.

question: What does 'Another screen loaded ... onto the machine' mean?
answer: Someone on another screen or browser tab loaded a different file onto the machine. The file shown on your screen isn't the one that would run, so load your file again if you want to cut it.
aliases: file loaded from another device warning
file shown is not the one that would run

question: What does 'Segment cap hit: downsampled' mean?
answer: Your file has more than 100,000 toolpath segments, so the app thinned out some display data to keep the 3D view responsive. The file itself and what's sent to the machine aren't changed.

question: Why is the line count on the file card different from my file?
answer: The file card doesn't count blank lines or comment-only lines. The machine reports its own count in the Console ("File loaded ... lines").

question: Can I load more than one file or queue jobs from the Sidebar?
answer: No. File Management holds one file at a time; loading another file replaces the current one, and dropping several files at once is refused.

question: Can I load a file while a job is running?
answer: No. Browse, drag and drop, Reload Current and Clear are locked while a job is running or paused, and the machine also refuses a new file with "A job is running. Stop it before loading another file." Stop the job first.

question: Can I load a G-code file from a USB stick?
answer: Yes, if the computer or tablet showing the app can see the drive. Click Browse for G-Code File and choose the file from the USB drive in the file picker.

question: Does the app handle inch G-code files?
answer: Yes. Files that use G20 (inches) are read, and the preview converts them to millimetres.

question: What's shown in the Position sub-tab?
answer: ZERO ALL and HOME ALL buttons, then a table with X, Y and Z rows showing Work Position and Machine Position, a mm/in units button, and small Zero (crosshair) and Home (house) icons on each row. An A row appears only when a rotary axis is connected.

question: How do I home the machine from the Sidebar?
answer: Go to Sidebar > Position and click HOME ALL, or press the Home key. HOME ALL is greyed out until the machine is connected.

question: Can I home a single axis from the Position tab?
answer: Each axis row has a small house icon ("Home X axis" and so on) that asks the controller to home only that axis. Not every controller responds to this button, so if nothing happens, use HOME ALL.

question: Why are ZERO ALL and HOME ALL greyed out?
answer: They're disabled until the machine is connected; connect on the Device tab and they become clickable. The per-axis Zero and Home icons stay clickable but do nothing while disconnected.

question: Can I zero or home while a job is running?
answer: Stop the job first. ZERO ALL and HOME ALL aren't locked on screen during a job, but zeroing or homing mid-job would change or lose the origin the job is using. Controllers that block this show "not available while a job is running" in the Console, and pausing isn't enough.

question: What is the A row in the Position table?
answer: It's the rotary A axis, shown in degrees, and it only appears when the controller reports a connected rotary axis. Its Zero and Home icons are greyed out because zeroing and homing the rotary axis aren't available yet.

question: What do the colored X, Y and Z badges mean?
answer: They're color-coded axis labels for quick reading: X is red, Y is green and Z is blue, and A is purple when a rotary axis is connected.

question: How many decimal places does the position readout show?
answer: Three decimals in millimetres and four in inches.

question: What does the ALARM or MOTOR ERROR banner in the Jog or Position tab mean?
answer: "ALARM — Machine locked" means the controller is in alarm and won't move until it's cleared. "MOTOR ERROR — Closed-loop error" means a motor driver reported a fault. Use the banner's buttons: Reset plus an axis resets that motor, and Reset All resets every motor and unlocks the machine.

question: What does Reset All do in the Sidebar alarm banner?
answer: It resets all motors and sends an unlock to clear the alarm, and the Console logs "Resetting all motors...". If the cause is still there, such as a triggered limit switch or a real motor fault, the alarm can come back.
aliases: clear all motor errors in sidebar

question: What's the difference between Reset Y1 and Reset Y2 in the Position tab?
answer: Both send a reset for the Y axis, so either one resets Y. The Jog tab's banner has a single Reset Y button instead.

question: Does keyboard jogging use the Speed buttons?
answer: No. Keyboard jogs use their own speeds, about 2000 mm/min for a single tap and 3000 mm/min while a key is held, whichever Speed button is selected. They do use the current Step (mm) size.

question: Why doesn't a quick second click on the jog dial move the machine?
answer: Jog clicks less than about 0.15 seconds apart are ignored to prevent accidental double moves. Wait a moment between clicks.
aliases: double click jog only moves once

question: Are my jog step and speed remembered?
answer: Yes. The selected Step (mm) and Speed are saved in this browser and come back after a reload. The defaults are 1 mm and Medium.

question: Does the Jog tab show my current position?
answer: No. The Jog sub-tab only has jog controls. Switch to the Position sub-tab or look at the bottom status bar to see coordinates.
aliases: where is position on jog screen

question: Why don't the arrow keys jog the machine?
answer: Arrow-key jogging only works when the machine is connected and no text field or dropdown has focus, so click an empty area first. Holding Ctrl or Alt also disables it. Jog moves are refused while a job is running or paused.

question: Why doesn't Space start my job?
answer: Space starts a job only when the machine is connected and idle, a file is loaded, and you're not typing in a field. If the machine is in alarm or a safety check is blocking the run, clear that first. Otherwise, hover over the Play (Start) button on the Carve tab to see why it's disabled.

question: Does pressing Escape to close something also stop my job?
answer: Yes. Whenever the machine is connected and you're not typing in a field, Escape sends a job Stop, even if you pressed it to close a camera view or another window. During a job, close windows with their close buttons instead.
aliases: escape closed camera and stopped job

question: Why did Ctrl+Z zero my machine instead of undoing?
answer: In this app, Ctrl+Z is the shortcut for zeroing all axes, not undo. It sets X, Y and Z to 0 at the current position immediately. If that was a mistake, jog back to your real origin and zero again, or probe again.
aliases: lost my origin with ctrl z

question: Why doesn't F5 or Ctrl+R refresh the page?
answer: The app blocks F5, Ctrl+R and Ctrl+Shift+R so the screen isn't reloaded by accident. If you really need to reload and your browser shows a reload button, use that; while the machine is connected or running, the browser asks you to confirm leaving.

question: Why can't I copy text or right-click in the app?
answer: Text selection, copying and the right-click menu are blocked everywhere except inside text boxes, so you can't copy lines out of the Console log. You can still paste into input fields.

question: Can I change or customize the keyboard shortcuts?
answer: No. The shortcuts are fixed, and there's no setting to change or turn them off.

question: Do keyboard shortcuts work on every tab?
answer: Yes. The jog keys, step keys, Space, Escape, Home and Ctrl+Z work on any top tab when you're not typing in a field. Ctrl+O is for the Prepare and Carve tabs, where it opens Browse for G-Code File.

question: Why does nothing happen when I click Connect Joystick?
answer: The browser has to detect the controller first: plug it in, press any button on it, then click Connect Joystick again. If it still fails, the error (such as "No gamepad/joystick detected") appears in the CNC Controller section of the Device tab, not in Joystick Control.

question: Why is Start Control greyed out?
answer: Start Control stays disabled until the CNC machine itself is connected. Connect in Device tab > CNC Controller, then go back to Joystick Control and click Start Control.

question: What do Standby and Active mean for the joystick?
answer: Standby means the gamepad is connected but won't move the machine. Click Start Control to switch to Active, so stick movements jog the machine, and click Stop Control to go back to Standby.
aliases: turn joystick jogging on and off

question: What do the gamepad sticks and buttons do?
answer: The left stick moves X and Y, and the right stick's up/down movement moves Z; the further you push, the faster it moves (roughly 500 to 2000 mm/min). The gamepad's buttons do nothing. The Left X, Left Y and Right Y (Z) bars show the live stick positions.

question: Why did my joystick stop working when I changed tabs?
answer: Joystick control only works while the Device tab is open. Leaving the Device tab disconnects the gamepad, so go back to Device > Joystick Control and click Connect Joystick and Start Control again.

question: Can I change the gamepad deadzone, speed or axis mapping?
answer: No. The app has no gamepad settings, so the stick mapping, speed range and deadzone are fixed. There's no Gamepad page under Settings.

question: How do I stop jogging with the gamepad?
answer: Let go of the sticks to stop sending moves, click Stop Control to return to Standby, or click Disconnect Joystick. In an emergency, use E-STOP on the Carve tab or your machine's physical stop.

question: Which gamepads work for jogging?
answer: Any gamepad or joystick your browser recognizes, such as common USB or Bluetooth game controllers. If several are connected, the first one the browser reports is used. If the browser doesn't support gamepads, you'll see "Gamepad API not supported in this browser".

question: Why doesn't my Console command do anything?

question: What does the '⛔ not available while a job is running' message mean?

question: Why won't Create Macro save?
answer: Both Macro Name and G-code Commands must be filled in; the form won't save if either one is empty.

question: What's the text under each macro name?
answer: It's a preview of the macro's first line (up to about 40 characters), so you can tell macros apart.

question: Can I export, import or share macros?
answer: No. There's no export, import or sharing for macros, and they aren't shared between screens or devices. Keep the G-code in a text file if you want to reuse it.

question: Why didn't my macro move the machine?
answer: Make sure the machine is connected (otherwise the play icon is greyed out) and not in alarm. Some controllers, such as RSP firmware, don't accept typed G-code lines, so macros have no effect on them. Check Sidebar > Console for errors after running the macro.

question: Can I stop a macro while it's running?
answer: There's no Stop button for macros. Once you click Run, every line is sent automatically about 0.1 seconds apart. To halt motion, click STOP on the jog dial, or use E-STOP on the Carve tab or your machine's physical stop.

question: How do I make the Sidebar wider or narrower?
answer: In the horizontal layout, drag the thin divider on the Sidebar's right edge (it highlights when you point at it) left or right. The width is remembered in this browser, within set minimum and maximum limits.

question: How do I reset the Sidebar or G-code panel width?
answer: Double-click the divider; its tooltip reads "Drag to resize · double-click to reset". The panel goes back to its default width and your saved size is forgotten.

question: How do I resize the G-code panel on the Carve tab?
answer: In the horizontal layout, drag the divider on the left edge of the G-code panel (to the right of the 3D view) left or right. The width is remembered in this browser, and double-clicking the divider resets it.

question: Why can't I resize panels on the vertical touchscreen layout?
answer: The vertical layout uses fixed columns: the Sidebar on the left, the 3D view on the right, and on the Carve tab the G-code panel under the 3D view. It has no drag dividers, so switch to the horizontal layout to resize panels.

question: How do I switch between horizontal and vertical layout?

question: Is my layout choice remembered?

question: Why can't I find the layout button?

question: What does the vertical layout look like?

question: Where is the E-Stop button and what does it do?
answer: The red E-Stop button is at the right end of the header, on every tab. It sends an emergency stop to the controller; on RSP controllers motion stops at once, the motor drivers are disabled, the position is kept, and a running job's resume line is saved. question: Why is the E-Stop button greyed out?

question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for E-Stop?

question: What does the status pill in the header mean?

question: What does INITIALIZING mean in the header?

question: What are the F and S numbers in the header?
answer: When connected, the header shows F with the current feed rate in mm/min and S with the spindle speed in RPM, next to the status pill. They're hidden in the vertical or touchscreen layout.

question: What happens when I click the firmware name in the header?

question: What does the Auto / Horizontal / Vertical layout button do?

question: How do I switch between dark and light theme?

question: Why can't I close the alarm popup?

question: What does the Clear Alarm button do?

question: Why doesn't Clear Alarm do anything?

question: What do the Reset X, Reset Y1, Reset Y2 and Reset Z buttons do?

question: What does Backend Online / Backend Offline mean on the Device tab?

question: How do I refresh the list of USB devices?

question: Why does it say 'No serial ports found'?
answer: The computer doesn't see a controller. Make sure it's powered and the USB cable is plugged in, try another cable or USB port, and check it appears in Windows Device Manager under Ports. Then click the refresh button on the Device tab.

question: Why can't I change the port, Baud Rate or Flow Control?

question: Why does the Device tab say 'Connected to device' instead of my port name?

question: Why did the app connect to the wrong device automatically?

question: How do I turn off auto-connect?

question: Which controllers does the app support?
answer: Device tab > CNC Controller > Connection Help lists GRBL, grblHAL, FluidNC and RTS/Buildbotics (RTS-1/RTS-2). The app also works with RSP controllers, whose firmware you can update in Settings > Hardware > Firmware.

question: What is the Machine Information box on the Device tab?

question: What do the dots on the Device tab section buttons mean?

question: How do I use a joystick or gamepad to move the machine?
answer: Plug in the gamepad, go to Device tab > Joystick Control and click 'Connect Joystick'. question: Why is Start Control greyed out in Joystick Control?

question: Why doesn't anything happen when I click Connect Joystick?

question: What do the $ numbers like $100 or $22 mean?

question: What does 'Changed only' do in the Firmware settings?
answer: Click 'Changed only' in the Device tab > Firmware toolbar to list only settings whose value differs from the default; the number in brackets is how many there are. Changed rows also get a dot marked 'Changed from default'.

question: What does 'Write N setting(s)' do?
answer: The bar above the Firmware list counts pending values; click 'Write N setting(s)' to send them all to the controller (connected only). Imported values are only sent when you click it. Values saved with Edit or Restore Defaults are already sent, so writing them again just repeats them.

question: Why are Read $$ and Edit greyed out?
answer: Read $$, Edit, Restore defaults and Write need a controller connection; while disconnected the Firmware section shows 'Not Connected'. Connect in Device tab > CNC Controller first. Export stays greyed out until settings are loaded.

question: What is the 'Other / Extended' group in Firmware settings?
answer: Settings your controller reports that aren't in the app's list appear under 'Other / Extended' as 'Setting $N' (extended or firmware-specific). You can still change them with Edit; their meaning depends on your firmware.

question: Can I edit a built-in machine profile?
answer: No, built-in profiles can't be changed or deleted, and custom profiles can't be edited after saving either. Click 'New Profile' in Device tab > Profiles and enter your own values instead.

question: Why is 'Apply to Controller EEPROM' greyed out?
answer: It needs a controller connection, and the Profiles panel shows 'Connect to your controller first to apply EEPROM settings.' Connect in Device tab > CNC Controller, then come back to Profiles.

question: Why is Export greyed out in Machine Profiles?
answer: Export only saves custom profiles, so it stays greyed out until you create one with 'New Profile' or import one.

question: Why doesn't HOME ALL do anything?
answer: HOME ALL is greyed out until you're connected. If it's clickable but nothing moves, clear any alarm first, and make sure no job is running or paused: homing isn't allowed until you stop the job, and the Console shows a '⛔ ... not available while a job is running' message.

question: Why didn't the homing progress window appear?
answer: The homing progress window only appears on controllers that report homing progress (RTS controllers). On other controllers homing still runs without it; watch the machine and the Console for messages.

question: How do I switch between millimetres and inches?
answer: Click the Units button in the bottom status bar to toggle mm and in; it also sends G21 or G20 to the controller. The mm/in button in the Sidebar Position tab's table header uses the same setting but only changes the readout. Device tab > Position (DRO) always shows mm.

question: What does 'Controller restarted — position lost' mean?

question: How do I clear the controller restarted warning so Start works again?

question: What happens if the USB cable disconnects during a job?

question: How do I update my controller's firmware?
answer: Connect the machine and make sure it's idle, then go to Settings > Hardware > Firmware. Click 'Check for updates', then 'Install Firmware Update (vX)' and confirm with 'Yes, Install Update Now'. Don't power off or unplug the machine while it shows 'Flashing Firmware...'.

question: Why is the Install Firmware Update button greyed out?

question: What does 'Check for updates' do?
answer: In Settings > Hardware > Firmware, it checks the internet for the latest official firmware and shows Current vs Latest with 'Update Available' or 'Up to Date'. '• Cloud OTA' appears when the info came from online; if the check can't reach the internet, it uses the release stored with the app.

question: What should I do after a firmware update?
answer: When it shows 'Firmware updated successfully!', the controller reboots, so reconnect once its port is detected, then click Done. Because the board restarted, you may see 'Controller restarted — position lost': home or re-zero X, Y and Z before running a job.

question: What if a firmware update fails?
answer: The log in Settings > Hardware > Firmware shows the error lines marked ✖, and a Try Again button appears. Official updates are checked against a SHA-256 checksum first, so a damaged download stops with 'SHA-256 integrity verification failed' before anything is flashed. Make sure the machine is connected and idle, then click Try Again.

question: What does 'Reinstall Firmware' mean?
answer: When your controller already has the latest version (Up to Date), the install button reads 'Reinstall Firmware (vX)' and flashes that same version again. It uses the same confirmation and rules as an update.

question: What is Developer Mode in Firmware & Updates?

question: Why does the app ask me to confirm when I close it?

question: Where should I place the bit before a Z Probe?

question: What does "probe rejected: ST_ERR_ESTOP" mean?

question: What does "probe rejected: ST_ERR_FAULT" mean?

question: What does "probe rejected: ST_ERR_BUSY" mean?

question: What does "move rejected" mean during probing?

question: What does "no reply for seq" mean during probing?

question: What does "Backend returned" or "Failed to fetch" mean in the Probing window?

question: Does the machine lift the bit after a failed probe?

question: Where is the Probing section in Settings?

question: What do the probe strategy cards in Settings do?

question: What do X-only (edge find) and Y-only (edge find) do?

question: Is remote access secure?

question: Where is the job control bar?
answer: On the Carve tab, along the bottom of the 3D view in the standard layout; in the vertical touchscreen layout it's the Job control card under the 3D view. It only appears once a file is loaded, or while a job is running or paused.

question: What do the buttons on the Carve tab's job control bar do?
answer: From left: Start/Pause (play icon), the progress readout, Run Outline (expand icon, traces the design's footprint at a safe height), Start From Line (skip-forward icon), Stop Job (square) and E-STOP. Hover over a button to see its name.

question: Why is the Start button greyed out?
answer: Start is disabled when the machine isn't connected, no file is loaded, the machine is in alarm, or the loaded file was refused as unable to run on this machine. Hover over it: a refused file shows "Cannot run:" with the line and reason, and the Console lists every problem.

question: What do Lines, Current and the percentage on the job control bar mean?
answer: Lines is the number of lines in the loaded file, Current is the line the machine has reached, and the percentage, with the progress bar under it, is how much of the job is done.

question: What does "continues from line N" on the job control bar mean?
answer: A stopped or interrupted job left a saved resume point (RSP controllers), so pressing Start continues from that line instead of the beginning. The tool first lifts, travels back to that spot and plunges before cutting; hover over Start to see the line and why the job stopped.
aliases: why does start say resume from line

question: How do I run my file from the beginning when Start keeps resuming from a saved line?
answer: The saved line (RSP controllers) is cleared when the job finishes normally or when a different file is loaded; loading the same file again keeps it. To start over from line 1, load another file and then load yours again. Running an outline also clears it.

question: What does the E-STOP button on the job control bar do?
answer: It stops motion immediately and disables the drivers, leaving the machine in an alarm/E-stop state. Check the machine, click Clear Alarm, and on RSP controllers Start then continues from the saved stop line. There's also an E-Stop button at the top right of the header.
aliases: what happens when I hit estop

question: What's the difference between Stop and E-STOP?
answer: Stop Job ends the job in a controlled way, and on RSP controllers the stop line is saved. E-STOP stops motion at once and disables the drivers, leaving the machine in alarm until you click Clear Alarm. Use E-STOP for emergencies and Stop Job for everything else.
aliases: difference between the two stop buttons

question: Why is the Stop button greyed out?
answer: Stop Job only works while the machine is connected and a job is running or paused. If the bar says "Connection to the machine lost", use the machine's own emergency stop.

question: What does "Connection to the machine lost" on the Carve tab mean?

aliases: connection lost warning on job bar

question: What does "Paused at line N" with a Resume button mean?
answer: The job reached a pause (an M0 or M1 in the program, or a check before lowering back into the cut) and every move before it has finished. Do what the message asks, for example start the spindle, then press Resume or Space to continue.

question: What does "Waiting at line N" with a Skip wait button mean?
answer: The file has a G4 dwell, so the machine is standing still on purpose for the time shown. It continues by itself when the wait ends, or press Skip wait to go on immediately.

question: Why is my job waiting several minutes at a G4 line?
answer: On RSP controllers the G4 time is read in seconds, so a post processor that writes milliseconds (for example G4 P2000) asks for a very long wait; the Console warns about waits of a minute or more when the file loads. Press Skip wait on the banner to continue.

question: Why didn't my job stop at the M0 pause in my file?
answer: On RSP controllers, M0 and M1 program pauses are skipped by default and the job runs straight through, so start your spindle before pressing Start. G4 dwells are still honoured, and there's no on-screen switch for this in the app.

question: Why does the job pause saying "Make sure the spindle is running at speed"?
answer: When you use Start From Line, or resume a stopped job, at a point where the file had the spindle on, the job holds with the tool at the start of that line (above the cut if it still has to lower) so you can confirm the spindle is running. Check it, then press Resume to continue.
aliases: why did start from line pause

question: Why won't my file run? It says it "cannot run on this machine".
answer: On RSP controllers the app checks every file when it loads and refuses one it can't run correctly; Start stays greyed out, its tooltip shows the first problem, and the Console lists the rest with line numbers. Common causes are a tool change after cutting has started, G55–G59 or G92 offsets, canned drilling cycles, cutter compensation, subprogram calls, a cutting move before any feed rate is set, or Z going higher than the machine can travel. Fix the file in your CAM software and load it again.

question: Can I run a file that has tool changes (M6)?

On other controllers the job holds at the M6 and the Console shows "Tool change requested", but this version has no on-screen button to confirm the change, so running one file per tool is the reliable approach.

question: How do I change bits between toolpaths?
answer: Save each tool's toolpaths as a separate file. When the first file finishes, change the bit, set Z zero again for the new bit (for example with Probe), load the next file and press Start, keeping the X and Y zero unchanged.

question: Why is my job running slower than the feed rate in my file?
answer: First check that Speed (Feed Override) in the Controls sub-tab isn't below 100%. On RSP controllers the app also caps feeds at the machine's maximum axis speeds and slows very short moves in fine 3D detail so the machine can follow them; the Console reports "Fine detail: slowed N short moves" when the file loads.

question: Why doesn't raising feed override above 100% speed up some moves?

question: How quickly does a feed override change take effect?

question: What is the range of the feed override?
answer: 10% to 200% of the programmed feed. -10% and +10% change it in big steps, -1% and +1% in small steps, and the reset button returns it to 100%.

question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for feed override?
answer: No, feed override has no keyboard shortcut; use the Speed (Feed Override) buttons in the Sidebar's Controls sub-tab.

question: Does the Space key start a job?
answer: Yes: when the machine is connected and idle with a file loaded, Space sends the file and starts it, from any tab. While a job runs Space pauses it, and while paused it resumes it. It does nothing while you're typing in a text box or when the machine is in alarm.

question: Why doesn't the Space key pause or start my job?
answer: Space is ignored while a text box has focus, so click on the 3D view first. It also does nothing when the machine isn't connected, is in alarm, or is idle with no file loaded.

question: Why does the play button show Start while my job is paused?

aliases: will start restart my paused job

question: What's the difference between Pause and Stop?
answer: Pause holds the machine where it is, and Start or Space carries on immediately from the same spot. Stop Job ends the job and unlocks file loading and the other tabs; on RSP controllers the stop line is saved so Start can continue later with a lift, return and plunge.

question: Does pausing a job turn off the spindle?
answer: No, Pause only holds motion; the app doesn't send a spindle-off with it. On RSP controllers the app doesn't control the spindle at all, so switch your router off by hand if you need it stopped.

question: What happens when my job finishes?
answer: The Console shows "Job completed", progress reaches 100%, and the header tabs, file loading and Jog unlock. On RSP controllers any saved resume line is cleared, so the next Start runs the file from the beginning.

question: Will refreshing the page or closing the browser stop my carve?

question: Why can't I load a new file during a carve?
answer: File Management is locked while a job is running or paused so the program can't be swapped mid-cut, and the Sidebar shows "Carve in progress — file and jog locked. Feed rate can be changed in Controls." Press Stop Job first, then browse for or drop the new file.

question: Can I load a different file while the job is paused?
answer: No, a paused job still counts as active, so File Management stays locked. Press Stop Job first; on RSP controllers loading a different file then clears the saved resume line.

question: Why is the Jog tab locked during a job?
answer: The job controls the machine while it runs, so the Jog sub-tab is locked ("Locked while carving") while a job is running or paused, and if you were on it the Sidebar switches to Controls. Stop the job to jog again; Position, Controls, Macros and Console stay available.

question: How do I start a job from a specific line?

question: What does Safe Z Height in the Start From Line dialog do?
answer: It's the height the tool travels at before lowering back into the cut, from 1 to 100 mm. On other controllers Z lifts to this height in machine coordinates before resuming.

question: What does the machine do when I press Start from Line?
answer: On RSP controllers it raises Z, moves to the X/Y where that line starts, lowers slowly (no faster than 300 mm/min) to that line's depth, then runs the rest of the file; the first note under Before you start describes these exact moves. question: Why is the "Start from Line" button greyed out in the dialog?
answer: It's disabled when the machine isn't connected or no file is loaded, when the chosen line can't be started safely (the reason is shown under Before you start), or when the machine position can't be trusted, for example after a controller restart. Re-zero X, Y and Z at the job's original origin (or home) if the notes ask you to, or pick a different line.

question: What does "No X/Y move happens before line N" mean?
answer: Nothing before that line moves X or Y, so the app can't work out where the tool should be and won't start there. If nothing has been cut yet, just press Start to run the file from the beginning; otherwise pick a line after the first X/Y move.

question: What does "Line N runs in incremental mode (G91)" mean?

question: What do "Last stop: line N" and "Use line N" mean in the Start From Line dialog?
answer: They show where the last stopped or interrupted job ended, why, and at what time. The Line Number defaults to that line; if you've changed it, click Use line N to go back to it.

question: What does the warning "The work zero was changed after this job stopped" mean?
answer: You zeroed or homed after the job stopped. Continue only if the zero is exactly the same origin the job started from; otherwise everything from that line on will be cut in the wrong place.

question: Why does Start From Line tell me to keep the existing zero?
answer: The rest of the cut is positioned from the zero the job started with, so re-zeroing now would shift everything still to be cut. Only re-zero if the position was lost, for example after a controller restart, and then at the job's original origin.

question: Why don't the line numbers in Start From Line match my file in a text editor?
answer: On RSP controllers the dialog counts the lines the machine actually runs: blank lines and comments are left out and arcs are converted into many short straight moves, so the numbers can differ from your original file. Use the G-code Context box to confirm you've picked the right spot.

question: Can I click a line in the G-code panel to start from there?
